import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    types = list(feats.types)
    x = feats.x
    y = feats.y
    
    # Remove highly correlated pairs (keep first in pair)
    keep = []
    seen = set()
    for i, id1 in enumerate(ids):
        if id1 in seen:
            continue
        keep.append(i)
        for j, id2 in enumerate(ids[i+1:], i+1):
            if id2 in seen:
                continue
            corr = np.corrcoef(x[:,i], x[:,j])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                seen.add(id2)
                break
    
    filtered_ids = [ids[i] for i in keep]
    filtered_x = x[:, keep]
    
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(filtered_ids):
        group0 = filtered_x[y==0, i]
        group1 = filtered_x[y==1, i]
        mean_diff = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
        effect_sizes.append(abs(mean_diff))
    
    # Select top features by effect size
    top_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
    top_features = [filtered_ids[i] for i in top_indices]
    
    # Check for interactions among top features
    products = []
    for i in range(len(top_features)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_features)):
            fid1 = top_features[i]
            fid2 = top_features[j]
            col1 = feats.column(fid1)
            col2 = feats.column(fid2)
            # Check if interaction term would be useful
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,col1], feats.x[:,col2])[0,1]) < 0.6:
                products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Build final design
    drivers = tuple(top_features[:min(len(top_features), MAX_DRIVERS)])
    columns = tuple(filtered_ids)
    products = tuple(products)
    
    # Create loadings using weighted sum of top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(filtered_ids):
        if fid in top_features:
            loadings[fid] = effect_sizes[i]
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
